packageRules.description: Owner 2026-10-21: Renovate merges its own green patch/minor PRs (fleet-gates SUCCESSFUL), at most one per run (the runner is hourly). Later rules switch it off for Symfony groups; majors are never automerged.

npm keeps its constraints and moves only package-lock.json when the new version is in range (package-lock.json has no content-hash tied to package.json, so a lock-only change stays consistent). Composer must NOT use update-lockfile: composer.lock carries a content-hash of composer.json, and a lock-only PR leaves it stale (FLE-130)
Symfony components (app/composer.json pins 8.1.*): one grouped PR for patch bumps, never merged by Renovate itself

Symfony constraints are wildcard series (8.1.*): replace them (8.1.* becomes 8.2.*, never an exact pin). Update-type rules cannot carry a rangeStrategy, so it sits here; patches are disabled below, only minor and major reach this

Symfony patch releases are not separate PRs (app/composer.json pins 8.1.*, so a patch needs no constraint change and a lock-only update would leave composer.lock content-hash stale, FLE-130): they arrive through the weekly lockFileMaintenance PR
Symfony minor bumps (8.1 -> 8.2) get their own PR: they change the pinned series and need a changelog read
Symfony major bumps get their own PR and are always a deliberate migration
Symfony UX (Twig components, Live components, Turbo, Icons, Stimulus bundle) release together: one grouped PR (rule order matters, this overrides the symfony groups above)
Doctrine ORM, DBAL, bundle and migrations: one grouped PR
PHP dev tooling (tests and static analysis): one grouped PR
Playwright and its axe-core integration (tests/playwright) move together; the companion's DDEV image pins the same Playwright version, so a bump here needs the matching companion change
Python CI tooling (ci/requirements-*.txt: pytest, jinja2, PyYAML, ansible-lint, ...): one grouped PR
Ansible Galaxy collections: one grouped PR
The OS image of the gates (debian:trixie) is a deliberate decision, in step with the servers: never auto-bump it
The Python interpreter version of the infra steps is a deliberate decision: never auto-bump the python docker image
The PHP platform constraint in app/composer.json is a deliberate decision: never auto-bump it
